how: data-spec (in the artifact and every static state) → the selector in src/journal that implements it. TWO independent axes: `status` = does the class/feature exist at the tree below (implemented | new | devtool); `visual` = does what exists match the design (aligned | divergent | unverified). A thing can be implemented and divergent — that combination is invisible to both the changelog's 'do not redo' list and its divergence list, so it gets its own field. `unverified` means settle it with the auto-diff, not by reading.

visualLegend.aligned: read the source and the design values agree
visualLegend.divergent: the class exists but its rendered treatment differs from the design — see note
visualLegend.unverified: not determinable from source reading; settle by probing design static vs live computed values

autoDiff.why: `implemented` is a statement about code existing, not about pixels matching. The only reliable arbiter is measuring both sides.
autoDiff.how: Run tools/probe.js against each static/*.html (design side) and against the live app with the same script (live side), keyed by data-spec → selector from this file. Diff per property.
autoDiff.tolerance: Exact match on colour/weight/size. ±1px on padding/height (subpixel + the app's 15px root). Ignore font-family when a fallback stack is in play.
autoDiff.expectation: Every `unverified` above resolves to aligned or divergent on the first run. Treat the output as both the work list and the regression gate.

granularity: Each data-spec is tagged on the SAME element the selector resolves to. Where a component needs several rungs (composer footer vs shell vs input; modal scrim vs card; row vs badge) each rung is its own spec/selector pair, so a diff never compares a container against a child. Fixed after the first auto-diff run reported mismatched granularity.
selectorProvenance: Every selector below was read from journal.pcss / components.tsx / context-menu.ts at the tree above. Entries whose selector could not be found in source are marked status:new with the name as an explicit `suggested` proposal — never asserted as existing. A previous revision of this file guessed `.mj_ContextMenu` for the menus; no such class exists and those entries are corrected here.
